cases.question: Show me US large-cap stocks trading under 12x earnings right now. Just the outright cheap ones on a P/E basis.

args.q: below a fixed number / less than a threshold

cases.result_summary: US large/mega universe=130; 5 matched pe<12, sorted asc: PBR 4.59, T, PGR, EQNR, COF. Absolute ceiling honored; pe served as trailing multiple.
cases.reason: Absolute P/E<12 ceiling, scoped US large-cap, market-wide (not hand-picked), trailing pe basis.

cases.question: I want European industrials that look cheap on EV/EBITDA compared with the rest of the industrials sector — below the sector average, not just below some fixed number.

args.q: below the sector average / cheaper than sector peers

cases.result_summary: EU industrials universe=448; 60 below sector-avg EV/EBITDA, ranked asc: CPPGroup, Mare Nostrum, Aumann, Norma, Fraport…
cases.reason: Cohort-relative (below_average vs gics:20 cohort), capital-structure-neutral EV/EBITDA, broad 448-name benchmark, Europe+industrials scope.

cases.question: Give me the cheapest decile of global tech stocks by price-to-free-cash-flow. I only care about the bottom 10% tail.

args.q: in the top decile highest 10 percent of the distribution

cases.result_summary: Global tech universe=4276; top-decile fcf_yield (=cheapest-decile P/FCF)=60 rows, ranked desc yield: Republic Power 14.4, Core AI 4.7, Truly Intl 2.2…
cases.reason: Cheapest decile served via the INVERSE (fcf_yield top-10% = P/FCF bottom-10%) over a broad 4276 global-tech universe; percentile framing honored.

defects.desc: No direct P/FCF valuation multiple exists in find_fsconcept (only fcf_yield, its reciprocal). Client must reason about the inversion and flip 'cheapest' to the top-yield tail — a stated P/FCF ask isn't directly executable.

cases.question: หาหุ้นถูกแต่คุณภาพดีให้หน่อย — P/E ต่ำ แต่ ROE สูงและหนี้ไม่เยอะ ไม่เอา value trap

args.q: debt to equity leverage low debt

cases.result_summary: Whole-market universe=24712; 60 matched low-PE + high-ROE + low-D/E. Quality gates present. (Extreme-tail sort surfaces micro-cap near-zero-PE distress names — screen logic sound, but a human would still eyeball those.)
cases.reason: Combines cheap multiple (low PE) WITH quality gates (high ROE, low leverage) in one screen — directly the anti-value-trap ask; Thai request addressed.

cases.question: Screen banks for me — P/B not P/E. US and European banks below 1x book, flag which have decent ROE so I'm not buying a broken bank.
cases.result_summary: US+EU banks universe=369; 74 below 1x book, ROE surfaced: e.g. NLB 0.23x/12.3% ROE (sound) vs many Crédit-Agricole regionals ~0.25x/2-3% ROE (cheap-for-a-reason).
cases.reason: P/B (not P/E) as primary bank multiple, sub-1x threshold, ROE paired for read-together sound-vs-impaired, US+Europe banks scope.

cases.question: Toyota vs the German automakers — is Toyota actually cheaper, or does it just look cheap because it reports in yen? Apples-to-apples multiple comparison.
cases.result_summary: USD-normalized multiples — Toyota pe 8.6 / EV/EBITDA 8.0 / pb 0.96 vs BMW 5.6/5.6/0.36, VW 7.0/3.7/0.19, Merc 8.5/8.3/0.47, Porsche 48/6.6/1.75. Toyota is NOT cheaper; the Germans are cheaper on every multiple. Tool's own guidance warns on same-basis/currency.
cases.reason: Ratio multiples are currency-neutral (and financials converts absolutes to USD); compares Toyota vs a set of 4 German automakers, refutes the yen-face-value illusion.

cases.question: Is Nestlé cheap versus its own history? Current P/E vs where it's typically traded over the past several years.
cases.result_summary: Current only: NESN pe≈27, ev_ebitda≈16, pb≈6.97. financials returns valuation multiples as latest-ONLY even with period=8y; asset_pulse's percentile_1y is a PRICE percentile, not a P/E-history percentile. No surface exposes the company's own multi-year P/E range/median.
cases.reason: Can state current P/E but the MCP exposes NO historical P/E series, so the own-history comparison the user asked for is not executable — correct behavior is to flag the limitation (not fabricate).

defects.desc: Valuation multiples (pe/ev_ebitda/pb) return only 'latest' — financials period param does not produce a per-year valuation-multiple history, and no other tool exposes a company's own multi-year P/E range/median/percentile. Own-history cheapness is unanswerable.

cases.question: Consumer staples in Asia cheaper than sector peers on P/E but still growing earnings — not cheap because shrinking.
cases.result_summary: Cheapness leg alone works (Asian staples universe=986, 40 below sector-avg PE). But adding the earnings-growth guard (net_income compound_growth) TIMES OUT twice (growth-series scan). Fallback net_income is_positive runs (48 matches) but only checks profitability, NOT growth — so the anti-shrinking condition (the point of the case) is unmet.
cases.reason: Sector-relative cheapness (vs gics:30 cohort, Asia) is correct, but the earnings-growth anti-value-trap leg times out; the only leg that completes doesn't distinguish growing from shrinking.

defects.desc: screen_unified times out (client read timeout, retried once) when a growth-series fundamental leg (net_income compound_growth) is combined with a cohort below_average leg over a broad universe. The known-slow growth-series scan makes the growth-guard un-runnable interactively.

cases.question: ช่วยหาหุ้นที่ PEG ต่ำกว่า 1 ในตลาดหุ้นสหรัฐ — ถูกเมื่อเทียบกับการเติบโต ไม่ใช่แค่ P/E ต่ำเฉยๆ

args.q: cheap relative to growth PEG ratio below 1

cases.result_summary: No 'peg' concept exists (find_fsconcept returns pe/normalized_pe/pb only) and no PEG pattern. A low-PE + earnings-CAGR surrogate is not a true PEG and cannot apply a PEG<1 threshold — and it also TIMES OUT (growth-series leg). PEG<1 is not expressible.
cases.reason: PEG is not a resolvable metric (no peg concept, no P/E-÷-growth relation), so PEG<1 cannot be applied; the growth-based surrogate also times out. US scope OK; core ask unmet.

defects.desc: No PEG metric or PEG-shaped relation is exposed (no 'peg' concept; relation form can't divide pe by an earnings-growth RATE). A first-class value-investor ratio (PEG) is missing from the fundamentals vocabulary.
The only PEG surrogate (pe + net_income compound_growth) also times out — same growth-series performance issue as vv-08.

cases.question: Shortlist of five oil majors comparing P/E — is five names enough to trust a 'peer average', or benchmark against the whole energy sector?
cases.result_summary: 5 majors ranked (USD): SHEL 10x (cheapest), TTE 11x, CVX 20x, XOM 21x, BP 21x. Robust benchmark available: whole energy-sector cohort=879 names, below-sector-avg PE screen returns 40 — so a 5-name avg is a thin/biased sample; the sector cohort is the proper reference.
cases.reason: Supports ranking the five AND benchmarking each vs the broad 879-name energy cohort (below_average vs gics:10); currency-consistent, sector-appropriate P/E + EV/EBITDA — enables the small-sample red-flag answer.

top_defects: No PEG metric/pattern exists (vv-09 FAIL) — a core value ratio (P/E ÷ growth) is unresolvable in find_fsconcept/find_fspattern.
No historical valuation-multiple series exposed (vv-07 PARTIAL) — financials returns pe/ev_ebitda/pb latest-only; 'cheap vs own history' is unanswerable.

screen_unified times out when a growth-series fundamental leg (net_income compound_growth) meets a cohort below_average leg (vv-08 PARTIAL, vv-09 surrogate) — the anti-value-trap growth guard is un-runnable interactively.
P/FCF only served via its inverse fcf_yield (vv-03) — no direct P/FCF multiple; client must flip the tail.
